title: Customer-Network-Safeguards-PRD-draft
content:
Status: Draft (working doc)
Owner: Aisha Patel (product)
Contributors: Marco Diaz (security), Sofie Nguyen (ops), Evan Walsh (serving-runtime)
---
High level: This PRD sketch captures a minimally viable set of safeguards, audit events, and approval gates for customer-managed networking used in Redwood Private deployments. The intent is to provide an operator-friendly onboarding flow that: (a) protects Redwood control plane and tenant isolation, (b) gives customers clear artifacts for their auditors, and (c) minimizes friction for self-service network handovers.

Goals (MVP):
- Define a compact audit event schema for all network handover and approval operations. Events must be sufficient for compliance audits (who/what/when/why, with cryptographic reference to config blobs).
- Establish an approval-gates matrix that surfaces required checks (security, connectivity, encryption, KMS access) and allows staged approvals (auto-approved, manual approver queue, emergency override with audit).
- Deliver an operator checklist/runbook for the self-serve VPC onboarding flow and for the Professional Services-assisted handover.
- Add lightweight telemetry that ties rollout status to customer IDs and surfaces per-customer failure modes (DNS, firewall, routing mismatches).

Out of scope for MVP:
- Full zero-trust attestation with HSM-backed signed manifests (future).
- Deep packet inspection or managed customer firewall changes (we only verify connectivity and policy adherence).

Assumptions:
- Customer provides a reachable control-plane endpoint or a set of IPs/subnets and BGP/peering details depending on connectivity mode.
- Customers have an existing KMS or integrate with Redwood KMS for secrets needed by agents.
- Legal/regulatory signoff may be required for certain regions (APAC deployments handled by separate legal flow).

User personas:
- Platform Engineer (customer): wants a checklist and an artifact to hand to their security/audit team.
- Redwood Solutions Engineer: facilitates initial onboarding and can trigger manual approvals if self-serve fails.
- Redwood SRE/operator: watches rollout telemetry and can quickly revert/failover if network causes control-plane instability.

Solution sketch
1) Handover artifact (single JSON manifest)
- A compact, verifiable manifest created by the customer (or generated via our self-serve UI) that contains: customer-id, network-mode (VPC-peering/VPN/DirectConnect), allowed subnet CIDRs, expected control-plane endpoints, cert thumbprints (optional), KMS reference (ARN), time-window for change, and a short business justification string.
- The manifest is stored in Redwood's config-store (immutable for audit) and referenced by a manifest-id in all subsequent events.
- TODO: prototype a manifest signed by customer GPG key for higher assurance (low priority).

2) Approval gates matrix (MVP)
- Gate A: Syntax/format validation (auto). Fails fast with clear error codes.
- Gate B: Connectivity verification (auto): Redwood attempts outbound/inbound checks from its test runners to the provided endpoints. Results recorded as separate audit events (tcp-syn, tls-handshake).
- Gate C: Policy compliance (semi-auto): check for overlapping subnets with other tenants, reserved IP usage, and required port openness. Auto-checks flag issues; manual review required for borderline cases.
- Gate D: Security signoff (manual): for networks that request elevated roles or cross-account IAM links. Approver=security@redwood or delegated SEs.
- Gate E: Final acceptance (auto if previous gates pass OR manual acceptance by SE). The outcome must be an explicit approval event with approver identity and manifest-id.

3) Audit logging schema (MVP fields)
All audit entries MUST include the following fields (flat, no nested):
- event_id (uuid v4)
- timestamp (iso8601)
- actor_name (string) - user or system component
- actor_type (user|system|se-automation)
- action (string) - e.g., manifest_uploaded, gate_connectivity_pass, gate_connectivity_fail, manual_approved, manual_rejected, rollback_triggered
- manifest_id (string) - manifest UUID referenced
- customer_id (string)
- region_hint (string) - e.g., us-west-2
- outcome (success|failure|warning)
- details (string) - freeform human text with reproducible steps or failure codes
- artifact_ref (string) - link to stored manifest or evidence blob (S3 path or internal ID)
- trace_id (string) - correlation id for debugging across subsystems
- signed_by (string) - if signed externally, name of signer (optional)

Note: For audit consumption by customer auditors we will provide an export tool that flattens events into a CSV/NDJSON with the fields above.

4) Evidence capture (telemetry + artifacts)
- For any connectivity gate attempt we capture: tcp-syn outcome, tls-handshake certificate chain (thumbprints only), packet-ttl results, traceroute summary, and a sha256 of the manifest used. Evidence is stored for 90 days (configurable for enterprise).
- Store a minimal packet-level transcript only when explicitly enabled during SE-assisted troubleshooting (opt-in) to avoid data sensitivity.

Onboarding checklist (operator-facing)
- Step 0: Create manifest in UI or upload via API -> manifest_id returned.
- Step 1: Automated validation run (Gate A) -> success/failure. If failure, return error with line numbers.
- Step 2: Kick off connectivity checks (Gate B) -> gather evidence. If failure, SE notifies customer to open required ports or provide alternate endpoints.
- Step 3: Policy cross-checks (Gate C) -> overlap/subnet/reserved ranges flagged.
- Step 4: If Gate C requires manual review or Gate D required, open approval ticket (auto-create JIRA INF-XXXX) and assign to security approver queue.
- Step 5: After approvals, Gate E applies final acceptance and manifests are marked active. Control-plane routes are updated in a canary-first manner (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%).
- Step 6: Post-handover audit export created and stored under the customer's evidence folder.

Runbook excerpt (failover)
- If after handover we observe >3% 5xxs to control-plane endpoints originating from customer region within 15 minutes, initiate rollback: mark manifest as revoked, revert routing, and notify both customer and SE team. Create incident and attach audit events.

Non-functional requirements
- Audit log write latency: <=2s for write acknowledgement after an action completes.
- Evidence retention: default 90 days, enterprise configurable to 365 days.
- Immutable manifest retention: 7 years for regulated customers (opt-in).
- Availability: rollout control-plane path should not reduce platform P99 SLA by more than 5% during a canary.

Acceptance criteria (MVP) - all must be true for GA:
- AC1: Upload and validation of a manifest (API + UI) works end-to-end with clear errors.
- AC2: Automatic connectivity check passes for a simulated customer VPC deployed in staging and evidence artifacts stored and replayable.
- AC3: Manual approval flow exists: approver can see evidence and approve/reject with a comment. Approval creates an immutable audit event.
- AC4: Rollback mechanism works via manifest revocation and route revert with audit trail.
- AC5: Audit export tool produces NDJSON with the required flat schema and matches evidence attachments.

Privacy & security notes
- Avoid storing customer-owned secrets in plaintext; references to external KMS or Redwood vaults must be stored as opaque identifiers only.
- Evidence blob access controlled by RBAC; support a read-only auditor role for customers.

Open questions / decisions
- Q1: Do we require customer-side signing of the manifest for GA? (Tradeoff: higher assurance vs. onboarding friction). Recommendation: optional for GA, mandatory later for higher tiers.
- Q2: Should we offer signed, time-limited pre-signed test connectors that customers run in their network for self-checks? (Helpful, but increases surface area).
- Q3: What SLA do we promise for manual security approvals? 48h? 24h? Recommendation: 24h for enterprise, 72h standard.
- Q4: Default evidence retention policy—90 days vs 180 days. Finance/Legal to finalize.

Implementation notes (engineering owners)
- Backend API: new /manifests endpoints (POST/GET/PUT revoke) with manifest store in encrypted S3 bucket; write audit events into our event-store (append-only) with immutability guarantees. Owner: backend team (Evan Walsh).
- Connectivity runner: small fleet in staging and production that performs tcp/tls/traceroute checks. Owner: infra/serving-runtime (Sofie Nguyen).
- UI: small manifest builder + approval queue view in Console. Owner: console/product (Aisha).
- Security: define approver roles and escalation flows (Marco Diaz).

Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (internal): implement manifest schema + local runner in staging. Do dry runs with SE customers (2 pilot customers).
- Phase 1 (pilot): expose self-serve to a limited cohort; require manual approvals by SEs. Collect feedback and tweak error codes.
- Phase 2 (GA): open to all Private customers; add tenant-level retention config and auditor role.

Next steps (short term)
- Action: create JIRA epic INF-4672 and attach this doc (Aisha).
- Action: Security to review audit schema and sign-off on evidence retention (Marco).
- Action: Infra to prototype the connectivity runner and report expected cost/ops delta (Sofie).
- Action: SE to line up 2 pilot customers willing to test the pilot flow (Evan).

Notes to self (TODOs)
- Add example manifest JSON and 2 example audit events to the doc (low-effort).
- Draft UI mock for manifest builder (wireframe).
- Confirm legal retention constraints per region.

End of draft.
